case.summary: Verdict: legitimate, fraud probability 0.03. The $125.08 online purchase (transaction 3509359, product R, region 264.0) on card C12265-K2 sits inside the card's normal history — home region, amount within its median-to-max range, familiar purchaser email — and the case-memory scorer rated it 0.006 despite a real-time risk_score of 0.52; the New device flag was a generic, widely-shared profile (253 cards all-time, zero fraud cases) rather than a ring signal, so pattern is none and there is no fraud episode (exposure $0.00). Because this was a single weak signal, R1 called for VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER before any block; the customer_validation request was asked and the assumed reply was a confirmation that the purchase was theirs (from a new device), which under R3 settles the case to ALLOW_TRANSACTION and CLOSE_NO_FRAUD, with a case opened per 3a for the evidence request. The eight retrieved similar cases (e.g. CC-5008, CC-4591, CC-3761, CC-3332, CC-4349, CC-4592) were all same-region alerts that cleared with pattern none, reinforcing this reading, though the card's two August confirmed-fraud account_takeover cases mean the alternative reading — treating any new-device online charge on this card as suspect — was not unreasonable, it just wasn't supported by any chain, ring, or shared-origin evidence here. Route: auto (no approval needed); had the customer instead denied the charge, R2 would have required BLOCK_CARD (L1) and CREATE_CASE.
